Two places in the REST module call `OrderService.getOrderTypes`, so a change to its behaviour could affect both. Both are in the `openmrs-module-webservices.rest` repository, under `omod/`. I found them with one repo-wide grep for `getOrderTypes(` and then read each call site. I did not check whether other code reaches `getOrderTypes` indirectly, for example through a helper or another service.

- **`OrderTypeResource1_10.doGetAll`** (lines 120-123) returns `getOrderTypes(context.getIncludeAll())` wrapped in `NeedsPaging`. This backs the `GET /ws/rest/v1/ordertype` list. Both the contents of the list and how many results come back depend on it.
- **`OrderTypeResource1_10.doSearch`** (lines 128-139) calls the same method with `context.getIncludeAll()`. It then removes any order type whose name doesn't match the `q` parameter, so the search results depend on the list `getOrderTypes` returns. It also removes items from the returned list in place, so it assumes that list is mutable.
- **`OrderableResource1_10.search`** (lines 64-70) calls `getOrderTypes(false)` and passes the result to `getOrderableConceptClasses(orderTypes)`. That decides which concept classes can be ordered, so a change would alter the results of the orderable concept search.

The remaining matches are in `OrderTypeController1_10Test.java` (lines 55, 99, 147 and 157). They are tests that would also be affected, but they aren't production code, so I left them out of the list below.
